Directions: Refer to the following list of demands made by the rebel leaders of the War of the Communities of Castile, a joint commoner-noble revolt against the heavy taxes imposed in Spain by Holy Roman Emperor Charles `text(V)` in `text(1520)`. Then answer each question that follows.
Content: “`ultext(Officials)`: When a Cortes [the traditional advisory council of Castile] must be called, `text(each district)` shall choose `text(two)` officials to go to the Cortes, `text(one)` from the nobility and `text(one)` from the commoners ... and `text(each bishopric)` shall choose `text(one)` cleric to go to the Cortes, and the knights shall choose `text(two)` knights, and the [religious] orders shall choose `text(two)` members of the orders, `text(one)` Franciscan and `text(one)` Dominican; and without all of these [representatives] there can be no Cortes.

`ultext(Justice)`: The king shall not be able to name a corregidor [district judge] in any place; instead, `text(each city)` and town shall on the `text(first day)` of the `text(year)` nominate `text(three)` nobles and `text(three)` commoners, and the king or his governor shall choose `text(one)` noble and `text(one)` commoner [from among these nominees]; these `text(two)` shall then be civil and criminal judges for `text(three years)`.
`ultext(Money)`: The king shall not be allowed to take any coins out of the kingdom, nor gold or silver dust, and no coin can circulate or have value in Castile if it was not minted in the kingdom.

`ultext(War)`: Whenever the king wishes to make war he shall summon a Cortes, and inform its members ... explaining the reasons for the war, so that they can see whether it is just or capricious. Without their consent the king cannot fight any war.”
